definitions.explanation: Information or news passed from person to person through spoken conversation rather than written communication.
The practice of passing down knowledge, stories, or techniques verbally from one generation to the next.

examples.japanese: ⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{口伝|くちづて}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{広|ひろ}まった→広まる：02404_hiromaru⟧。
examples.english: That shop became popular through word of mouth.

examples.japanese: {口伝|くちづて}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{聞|き}いた→聞く：00483_kiku⟧⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧だ⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、⟦{正確|せいかく}→正確：03372_seikaku⟧⟦かどうか→かどうか：28299_kadouka⟧わからない。
examples.english: I heard it through word of mouth, so I'm not sure if it's accurate.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦レストラン→レストラン：01048_resutoran⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{口伝|くちづて}⟦だけ→〜だけ：03093_dake⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{予約|よやく}→予約：01522_yoyaku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧いっぱい⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: That restaurant fills up with reservations through word of mouth alone.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{技術|ぎじゅつ}→技術：01389_gijutsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{口伝|くちづて}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{伝|つた}えられて→伝える：01220_tsutaeru⟧きた。
examples.english: This technique has been passed down through oral tradition.

examples.japanese: ⟦{文字|もじ}→文字：03632_moji⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦なかった→ない：01118_nai⟧⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{歴史|れきし}→歴史：02267_rekishi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{口伝|くちづて}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{次|つぎ}→次：00819_tsugi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{世代|せだい}→世代：05102_sedai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{伝|つた}えられた→伝える：01220_tsutaeru⟧。
examples.english: In the era before writing, history was passed to the next generation through oral tradition.

examples.japanese: ⟦{師匠|ししょう}→師匠：12421_shishou⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{弟子|でし}→弟子：03986_deshi⟧⟦へ→へ：02473_he⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{口伝|くちづて}⟦によって→によって：06801_niyotte⟧、⟦{伝統芸能|でんとうげいのう}→伝統芸能：15098_dentougeinou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{守|まも}られて→守る：01986_mamoru⟧きた。
examples.english: Traditional performing arts have been preserved through oral transmission from master to apprentice.

notes:
Emphasizes that information travels through spoken word rather than written or digital means. The same kanji {口伝|くでん} read as くでん refers specifically to secret oral teachings in traditional arts or religion, while くちづて is the everyday word for word-of-mouth communication.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {口伝|くちづて}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{広|ひろ}まる→広まる：02404_hiromaru⟧: to spread by word of mouth
- {口伝|くちづて}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{聞|き}く→聞く：00483_kiku⟧: to hear through word of mouth
- {口伝|くちづて}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{伝|つた}える→伝える：01220_tsutaeru⟧: to pass on orally
- {口伝|くちづて}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{伝|つた}わる→伝わる：01961_tsutawaru⟧: to be passed down orally

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {口伝|くでん}: secret oral teachings transmitted within a tradition (more formal, specialized)
- ⟦{口コミ|くちこみ}→口コミ：17690_kuchikomi⟧: word-of-mouth reviews or recommendations, especially for products and restaurants (modern, casual)
- ⟦{伝聞|でんぶん}→伝聞：17978_denbun⟧: hearsay; information received secondhand (more formal, often used in legal or journalistic contexts)
